items.title: Ext groups before and after reduction modulo the powers of an ideal are pro-isomorphic

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I in a Noetherian ring A and finite modules M and N, sets A_n = A/I^n, M_n = M/I^nM and N_n = N/I^nN, and asserts that for every i >= 0 the systems {Ext^i_A(M, N)/I^n Ext^i_A(M, N)} and {Ext^i_{A_n}(M_n, N_n)} are isomorphic in the category C of weird systems (source lines 29193-29210). The proof is a long comparison argument. It first chooses a presentation 0 -> K -> A^{oplus r} -> M -> 0, defines K_n = K/I^nK and K(n) = Ker(A_n^{oplus r} -> M_n), and uses the Artin-Rees consequence lemma to get a constant c and maps K(n) -> K_n/I^{n-c}K_n that are 'almost inverse', exhibiting an isomorphism of the systems (K(n)) and (K_n) in C (proof lines 29213-29229). It then proves the analogous statement for Ext groups: the surjections K_n -> K(n) have kernels annihilated by I^c, so the induced maps on Ext have kernel and cokernel annihilated by I^c, giving an isomorphism of the two Ext systems by the comparison lemma (proof lines 29232-29244). The proof then reduces to i = 0, 1 by the shift isomorphisms Ext^{i-1}_A(K, N) = Ext^i_A(M, N) and the analogous statement after reduction (proof lines 29247-29254). The substantive part is the final diagram chase for i = 0, 1: the proof writes down the commutative diagram comparing the two long exact sequences, uses the Mittag-Leffler comparison lemma to bound the kernel and cokernel of Hom(M, N)/I^n Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M_n, N_n) and of the analogous map for K by I^c-torsion, constructs maps delta_n between the I^c-saturated pieces, and finally makes a diagram chase (stated to be omitted) on the displayed solid diagram to define the dotted arrow and bound its kernel and cokernel (proof lines 29257-29304). The two-step reduction with Artin-Rees, the annihilation bookkeeping with a single constant c, and the final chase are independent research-level content.
